result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a marked continental crosswalk and continuous sidewalks, but lacks essential accessibility features like curb ramps. The crossing is uncontrolled and sightlines are partially obstructed by parked vehicles along the curb.

hazards.name: Lack of curb ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left terminates in a vertical curb without a ramp, creating a significant barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground at the start of the crosswalk

hazards.name: Uncontrolled crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks any traffic control devices like stop signs or signals, requiring pedestrians to rely on driver yielding behavior.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image across the roadway

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars on the right side of the street are positioned close to the crosswalk, potentially hiding pedestrians from oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the crosswalk

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at all corners of the intersection to ensure accessibility for all users.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to sidewalk level to slow traffic and increase pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, sidewalks, and signalization. However, the environment is dominated by wide asphalt surfaces and lacks physical traffic calming measures or greenery. This design prioritizes vehicle throughput over pedestrian comfort and safety.

hazards.name: Wide turning radii
hazards.description: The intersection corners allow for high-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection, including a delivery truck, obscure sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the side street

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten crossing distances and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Add trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and overhead traffic signals on a one-way street. However, it lacks dedicated pedestrian signals, ADA-compliant curb ramps, and physical buffers between the sidewalk and the roadway, creating a basic but unprotected environment.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: Pedestrians must rely on vehicle traffic lights, which may not provide adequate time or clear indication for crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk limit sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Missing Curb Ramps
hazards.description: Lack of sloped transitions makes the crossing inaccessible for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk in the foreground

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated signals to provide clear crossing intervals for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Daylighting with Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the intersection and extend the curb to improve visibility and shorten crossing distance.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install standard curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points.

result.summary: The image shows a one-way urban street with sidewalks on both sides and a marked crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps is present, the crosswalk markings are faded and there is a lack of pedestrian-specific signage or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The continental-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street are positioned close to the intersection, potentially blocking the view between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the crosswalk

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and further improve visibility.
